title: Case study: FMEA risk on a pilot submission
text: Mitigation point exercise. Suppose team addresses two highest-RPN risks: add missing SDTM variables document ADaM derivation, lowers probability detectability difficulty. apply_mitigations() takes updates recomputes RPNs levels.
code: ranked <- rr[order(-rr$rpn), c("risk_id", "description", "rpn", "risk_level")] head(ranked, 3) #> Warning: Unknown or uninitialised column: `status`. #> ℹ Risk Register: 3 risk(s), 0 open #> ℹ   Critical: 0, High: 3, Mean RPN: 48 #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   risk_id  description                                           rpn risk_level #>   <chr>    <chr>                                               <dbl> <chr>      #> 1 RISK-006 Laboratory units not standardized across sites         48 high       #> 2 RISK-008 Traceability gap: ADLB.BASE derivation undocumented    48 high       #> 3 RISK-013 Incomplete audit trail for manual data corrections     48 high top_two <- head(ranked$risk_id, 2)  updates <- data.frame(   risk_id       = top_two,   probability   = c(1, 2),   detectability = c(1, 1),   status        = "mitigated",   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  rr_after <- apply_mitigations(rr, updates)

title: Risk Management with r4subrisk
text: FMEA (probability times impact times detectability) default, scoring rule pluggable. risk_model_probability_impact() drops detectability two-factor matrix, risk_model_ich_q9() gives qualitative acceptable, tolerable, unacceptable ranking. model normalizes 0-100 score, Risk pillar consumes way. use rule, build risk_model() scoring function, maximum raw score normalization, level bands:
code: risks <- data.frame(   risk_id = c("R001", "R002"),   description = c("Missing vars", "Bad derivation"),   probability = c(4, 3), impact = c(5, 4), detectability = c(2, 3) )  apply_risk_model(risks, risk_model_probability_impact()) #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   risk_id raw_score risk_score risk_level model              #>   <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>      <chr>              #> 1 R001           20         80 critical   probability_impact #> 2 R002           12         48 high       probability_impact apply_risk_model(risks, risk_model_ich_q9()) #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   risk_id raw_score risk_score risk_level   model  #>   <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>        <chr>  #> 1 R001            9      100   unacceptable ich_q9 #> 2 R002            6       66.7 unacceptable ich_q9 impact_only <- risk_model(   name = "impact_only",   score = function(df) df$impact,   max_raw = 5,   bands = list(high = c(4, 5), medium = c(3, 3), low = c(1, 2)),   required = "impact" ) apply_risk_model(risks, impact_only) #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   risk_id raw_score risk_score risk_level model       #>   <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>      <chr>       #> 1 R001            5        100 high       impact_only #> 2 R002            4         80 high       impact_only

what: r4subrisk: Risk Quantification Engine for Clinical Submission Readiness — r4subrisk-package
title: r4subrisk: Risk Quantification Engine for Clinical Submission Readiness — r4subrisk-package
text: Quantifies submission risk using Failure Modes Effects Analysis (FMEA)-inspired framework (probability, impact, detectability). Builds risk registers evidence, computes Risk Priority Numbers (RPN), classifies risk levels, emits standardized R4SUB (Ready Submission) evidence table rows via 'r4subcore'. Supports risk mitigation tracking trend analysis across submission milestones.

title: r4subrisk: Risk Quantification Engine for Clinical Submission Readiness — r4subrisk-package
text: Maintainer: Pawan Rama Mali prm@outlook.(ORCID) [copyright holder]

title: Default Risk Configuration — risk_config_default
text: rpn_bands Named list RPN band boundaries c(lower, upper). Evaluated order; first match wins. evidence_severity_to_probability Named numeric vector mapping evidence severity probability scores (1–5 scale). evidence_severity_to_impact Named numeric vector mapping evidence severity impact scores (1–5 scale). default_detectability Default detectability score (1–5) explicitly provided. Lower = detectable.

title: Default Risk Configuration — risk_config_default
text: list class "risk_config" elements: rpn_bands, evidence_severity_to_probability, evidence_severity_to_impact, default_detectability.

title: Default Risk Configuration — risk_config_default
text: FMEA-inspired risk model uses three dimensions: Probability (1–5): likelihood issue occurring/persisting Impact (1–5): severity consequence unresolved Detectability (1–5): difficulty detecting issue (1 = easy, 5 = hard) RPN = Probability x Impact x Detectability (range 1–125)

title: Monte Carlo Uncertainty on Risk Priority Numbers — risk_monte_carlo
text: FMEA scores risk single integer values probability, impact, detectability, assessments judgements uncertainty. simulation treats score uncertain, draws many possible registers, reports resulting distribution Risk Priority Numbers, per risk register whole. turns single RPN range probability critical, risk review actually wants know.

title: Monte Carlo Uncertainty on Risk Priority Numbers — risk_monte_carlo
text: register risk_register create_risk_register(), data.frame risk_id, probability, impact, detectability. n Number Monte Carlo iterations. Default 10000. spread Standard deviation per-component uncertainty, scale points. Default 1. Use 0 deterministic result. config risk_config risk_config_default(), used critical threshold. seed Optional integer seed. supplied random state set call restored exit, result reproducible without disturbing caller's RNG stream.

title: Monte Carlo Uncertainty on Risk Priority Numbers — risk_monte_carlo
text: list class "risk_monte_carlo" n, spread, crit_threshold, point_total (deterministic register RPN), total (named numeric summary total RPN distribution), total_draws (simulated totals, plotting), per_risk (data.frame risk_id, rpn, mc_mean, mc_sd, p05, p50, p95, prob_critical).

title: Monte Carlo Uncertainty on Risk Priority Numbers — risk_monte_carlo
text: draw, every FMEA component sampled normal distribution centred assessed value standard deviation spread (scale points), rounded clamped 1–5 scale. spread = 0 reproduces deterministic RPN. per-draw RPN probability * impact * detectability, register total sum. critical threshold lower bound top RPN band config.

title: Monte Carlo Uncertainty on Risk Priority Numbers — risk_monte_carlo
code: risks <- data.frame(   risk_id = c("R001", "R002", "R003"),   description = c("Missing SDTM vars", "Unmapped derivations", "Define drift"),   probability = c(4, 3, 2), impact = c(5, 4, 3), detectability = c(2, 3, 4) ) rr <- suppressMessages(create_risk_register(risks)) mc <- risk_monte_carlo(rr, n = 2000, seed = 1) mc$total #>  mean    sd   p05   p50   p95   min   max  #>  96.1  32.0  50.0  92.0 156.0  21.0 230.0  mc$per_risk #>   risk_id rpn mc_mean mc_sd p05 p50 p95 prob_critical #> 1    R002  36    35.1  19.8   9  32  75         0.048 #> 2    R001  40    36.9  19.2  12  34  75         0.031 #> 3    R003  24    24.1  15.5   6  20  50         0.011
